title: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science - Pre Vocational Studies - Crop Propagation and Cultural Practices
exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In agriculture, the process of increasing the number of plants of a particular species is defined as ________.
questions.explain: Propagation means to reproduce, multiply, or increase the number of plants, either sexually (by seeds) or asexually (by vegetative parts).
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The method of crop propagation that involves the use of seeds, which are the products of fertilization, is called ________.
questions.explain: Sexual propagation involves the fusion of male and female gametes to produce seeds, which are then planted to grow into new plants.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Propagation of crops using vegetative organs such as stems, leaves, or roots is an example of ________.
questions.explain: Asexual propagation does not involve male and female gametes. Instead, it relies on vegetative parts of a parent plant to grow a new, genetically identical plant.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following crops is exclusively propagated asexually using stem cuttings?
questions.explain: Cassava is mostly grown vegetatively by cutting its mature stems and burying them in the soil to sprout into new plants.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: One major advantage of propagating crops by seed (sexual propagation) is that seeds ________.
options: Always grow much faster than vegetative organs
Are usually bulky and hard to carry
Can be easily stored and transported over long distances
Produce plants completely identical to the parent plant without variations
questions.explain: Seeds are generally small, light, and have low moisture content, making them very easy and cheap to store and transport compared to bulky vegetative parts like tubers or stems.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A known disadvantage of sexual propagation (by seed) is that the resulting offspring ________.
options: May not exhibit the exact characteristics of the parent plant
Always die within the first week of germination
questions.explain: Because sexual propagation involves the mixing of genes from two parents, the resulting offspring may show variation and not be true-to-type (identical) to the original parent.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of vegetative propagation over seed propagation?
options: It causes genetic variation in plants
It produces plants that mature and bear fruits earlier
Vegetative materials are easier to store than seeds
It requires the presence of pollinating insects
questions.explain: Plants propagated vegetatively (asexually) typically bypass the early seedling stages and mature faster, thereby bearing fruits earlier than plants grown from seeds.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is a significant disadvantage of vegetative propagation?
options: The planting materials are often bulky and difficult to transport
The offspring produced are genetically superior to the parents
It is completely impossible to perform on fruit trees
It introduces diseases that affect seeds only
questions.explain: Vegetative materials such as yam setts, cassava stems, and suckers are very bulky, heavy, and have a high moisture content, which makes their transportation and long-term storage difficult.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Grafting and budding are advanced examples of ________ propagation used extensively for fruit trees.
questions.explain: Budding and grafting involve joining vegetative parts (scion and rootstock) of two different plants to grow as one, classifying them as methods of asexual/vegetative propagation.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which method of propagation would a farmer choose if the main goal is to maintain the exact genetic uniformity (clones) of a highly yielding crop?
questions.explain: Vegetative propagation is the only method that guarantees clones—offspring that are 100% genetically identical to the parent plant, because no gene mixing occurs.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
